name: Fadrozole

lead: Fadrozole (Afema) is an oral aromatase inhibitor used for breast cancer in Japan. Outside oncology it mainly appears in animal and lab research as a way to block estrogen production.
No human trial has examined it for appearance.

paras: It reversibly binds the heme group of aromatase, reducing conversion of androgens to estrogens by about 80 to 90 percent at tested doses.
The sources reviewed do not detail its side effects. It is prescription-only and not approved in most countries.

lead: Fadrozole (brand name Afema, Novartis) is a selective, nonsteroidal, oral aromatase inhibitor that is or has been used in Japan for breast cancer.[1] It is classed as a Type II (reversible) inhibitor that binds the heme group of the aromatase enzyme.[1]

Most published work on fadrozole beyond oncology is laboratory research in which it is used as a tool to block estrogen synthesis in fish, birds and rodents. No published human trial has tested it for appearance outcomes.

paras: Fadrozole has been used for estrogen-dependent breast cancer in Japan.[1] A 1992 study tested it in postmenopausal women with advanced metastatic breast cancer.[1]

In comparison tables of aromatase inhibitors, fadrozole at 1 mg daily reduced aromatase activity by about 82 percent in postmenopausal women, and 2 mg twice daily by about 93 percent, placing it in the second generation with lower inhibition than anastrozole, letrozole and exemestane.[1] A 1991 Journal of Medicinal Chemistry paper described it as a potent, selective nonsteroidal inhibitor.[1]

Fadrozole has been used experimentally to inhibit aromatase in animals, including studies of fathead minnow reproduction, zebrafish gonadal differentiation and sex reversal in fish, and of neuroprotection by brain aromatase.[2][3][4][5][6]

Human clinical work is in breast cancer, including a meta-analysis of aromatase inhibitors in advanced disease and studies of HER-2 levels and response to hormone therapy.[7][8][9] No studies were found testing fadrozole for appearance, muscle or body composition.

timeline.event: Fadrozole hydrochloride described as a potent, selective nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor.[1]
